title: Capability contract and version routing for model onboarding
creator: Asha Patel
description: Introduce a unified capability contract (v2 envelope) surfaced by the model manifest/profile APIs and add routing rules for version pinning and graceful fallback. This ticket covers the API schema additions, migration plan for existing model manifests, server-side routing logic, and console display changes so customers can see guarantees (context window, token limits, supported features, perf estimates).
acceptance_criteria: New /models/manifest and /models/profiles endpoints return a 'capability_contract_v2' object for all newly onboarded models

Client SDKs can request capability_contract_v2 and receive fields: max_context_tokens, recommended_max_inference_tokens, supported_features (streaming,tool_calling,embeddings), perf_profile (p50_latency_ms, tokens_per_sec_estimate), quantization_profile
Version pinning routing accepts 'model:alias@version' and falls back to a compatible variant when the exact variant is unavailable; fallback rules are deterministic and documented
Migration: existing manifests are backfilled with capability_contract_v2 defaults and flagged; no runtime regressions observed in canary (latency/throughput within 5% of baseline)
Console surfaces the capability contract with a changelog link and a toggle to opt into strict version pinning; product approved UX copy
Automated integration tests validate routing behavior across three failure modes: variant OOM, cluster capacity constraint, and incompatible feature (e.g., streaming missing)
Performance dashboard shows before/after p50 and throughput estimates for 5 representative models after rollout
tasks: Design JSON contract: capability_contract_v2 schema (fields, units, semantics)
Backend: extend model manifest service to persist and serve capability_contract_v2
Routing: implement version-aware resolver with fallback policy and compatibility checks
SDKs: update Python/TS SDKs to surface new fields and helper for pinning
Console: add read-only view + opt-in strict pinning toggle
Migration: write backfill job and run on staging + production canaries
Tests: unit, integration, and load tests to exercise routing and perf annotation
Docs: publish Confluence spec and update public API changelog
decisions: Use 'capability_contract_v2' as the top-level key to avoid breaking v1 consumers
Represent latency estimates as p50 in milliseconds and throughput as tokens_per_sec_estimate (90th percentile traffic mode)
Fallback policy: prefer same-architecture variants, then lower-quantization variants, then regional replicas; explicit opt-in for cross-architecture fallback
Version pinning semantics: 'alias@semver' will match the exact semver if available; otherwise, follow fallback policy. Strict pinning flag enforces exact-match or 412 response
Quantization_profile will be a stable token in the contract (e.g., 'q4_0', 'q8_0'), not an opaque binary blob
implementation_plan: Week 1: Finalize schema and update manifest service contract; create migration backfill framework
Week 2: Implement routing resolver and unit tests; SDK stubs for capability_contract_v2
Week 3: Run staging backfill, integration tests, and performance canary on 10% traffic
Week 4: Rollout to 50% with monitoring alerts, then full rollout pending no regressions
risks: Backfill may produce inconsistent manifests for older models - mitigate with validation job and rollback path
Fallback to lower-precision variants could change output quality - require signal in perf_profile and product approval
Increased API payload size may marginally affect cold-call latency for manifest-heavy flows
test_plan: Unit tests for schema validation and backwards compatibility with v1 consumers
Integration tests covering routing: exact-match, architecture-fallback, quantization-fallback
Load test to ensure manifest service QPS at 5x expected production read rate
Canary monitors: p50 latency, tokens/s, error rate, and correctness smoke tests against reference prompts
notes: UX copy for strict pinning toggle pending PM sign-off (PM provided an initial draft)
We debated embedding perf curves vs. single-number estimates; opted for single-number tokens_per_sec_estimate plus optional serialized benchmark link
Performance numbers should be labeled with measurement conditions (sequence length, batch size); include in perf_profile.metadata
